L69: ## Why Get Certified?
L70: 
L71: Certified Data Centers receive visible trust signals and algorithmic advantages on the Vast platform.
L72: 
L73: ### Blue Trust Label
L74: 
L75: Your offers display a verified blue label on the platform, signaling professional-grade infrastructure to renters.
L76: 
L77: ### Priority Placement
L78: 
L79: Certified machines are auto-sorted higher in search results, so enterprise customers find you first.
L80: ### Increased Traffic
L81: 
L82: We actively direct more user flow to certified hosts because of the quality and reliability of their equipment.
L83: 
L84: ### Dedicated Support
L85: 
L86: Get direct access to the Vast team for onboarding, troubleshooting, and operational support.
L87: 
L88: ## What It Takes
L89: 
L90: You provide GPU hardware in a professional environment. Vast.ai lists your machines with a blue trust label and prioritizes them on the platform. Clients rent your GPUs, and you earn based on usage.
L91: ### Professional Environment
L92: 
L93: Servers housed in a professionally managed data center facility with reliable power, cooling, and network infrastructure.
L94: 
L95: ### Minimum 5 GPU Servers
L96: 
L97: At least 5 servers equipped with flagship-class GPU hardware (e.g. A100, H100, H200, RTX 4090/5090).
L98: 
L99: ### Verified Business
L100: 
L101: Equipment owned by a registered business. Owners must complete identity verification and sign the Data Center Hosting Agreement.
L102: ### Security Standards
L103: 
L104: Certifications like ISO 27001, SOC 2, or equivalent are encouraged and will strengthen your application, but are not strictly required.
L105:

L118: # Hosting Overview
L119: 
L120: Copy page Copy page
L121: 
L122: Vast is a GPU marketplace. Hosts sell GPU resources on the marketplace. Hosts are responsible for:
L123:   * Setup: installing Ubuntu, creating disk partitions, installing NVIDIA drivers, opening network ports on the router and installing the Vast hosting software.
L124:   * Testing and troubleshooting all issues that can arise, such as driver conflicts, errors, bad GPUs, and bad network ports. Vast does not offer support for getting your machine working. Connect your Vast host account to our Discord to access our cite90†host-only discord channels†discord.gg to chat or seek help from other hosts on the platform.
L125:   * Managing your offers, including pricing and offer end dates
L126:   * Planning maintenance so that no active rental contracts are disrupted

L128: 
L129: cite49†​ L130: 
L131: Account setup and hosting agreement
L132: You must create a new account for hosting. If you are using Vast.ai as a client, do not use the same account. A single client and hosting account is not supported and you will quickly run into issues. Once your account is created, open the cite91†host setup guide†cloud.vast.ai . There is a link in the first paragraph to the hosting agreement. Read through the agreement. Once you accept, your account will then be converted to a hosting account.
L133: You will notice there is now a link to Machines in the navigation, along with some other changes. Your account can now list machines that are running the daemon software.
L134: ##
L135: 
L136: cite50†​ L137: 
L138: Machine setup
L139: 
L140: The cite91†host setup guide†cloud.vast.ai is the official documentation for setting up a machine on Vast.ai. Read through each section closely. Common issues to check:
L141:   * Make sure to test the networking. Clients require open ports to directly connect to the machine for most jobs.
L142:   * Make sure to read the section on IOMMU if you have an AMD EPYC system.
L143:   * Make sure to disable auto-updates so that your machine doesn’t drop a client job to update a driver.
L144: Once you are ready to list your machine, come back to this guide to understand pricing and the rental contract lifecycle.
